themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints exploded to 37 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1873% spike (z-score: 25.76)—suggesting a sudden cluster of code violations, illegal conversions, or unsafe occupancies in Greenwich Village/SoHo that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 37 Building/Use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over 8-week baseline (1873% increase, z-score: 25.76)
Spike is concentrated in the current reporting week, not a gradual trend
High z-score indicates extreme statistical anomaly, not random variation
reporting_angles: Contact DOB to identify which specific buildings triggered complaints; inspect for illegal residential conversions, unlicensed commercial uses, or overcrowding in the district
Interview residents and building owners in affected blocks to understand what prompted the sudden spike in complaints this week

themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street Condition complaints jumped to 47 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 19.4 weekly average—a 143% spike (z-score: 4.26)—indicating accelerating pothole, pavement, and sidewalk failures across the district that align with community board's long-standing demands for street reconstruction.
evidence: 47 Street Condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (143% increase, z-score: 4.26)
Spike emerged in the current week, not weeks ago
Community board has repeatedly requested street reconstruction/upgrade in budget submissions, indicating chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Map the 47 complaints to identify geographic hotspots; photograph worst potholes and sidewalk damage for visual storytelling
Query DOT on repair timeline and budgetary constraints; tie to community board's unfunded infrastructure requests

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Proliferate
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned Vehicle complaints surged to 11 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 2.1 per week—a 418% spike (z-score: 9.57)—signaling a new or concentrated problem in parking enforcement and vehicle removal that emerged within the past 7 days.
evidence: 11 Abandoned Vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly baseline (418% increase, z-score: 9.57)
Spike is acute and current-week focused, not sustained over weeks
Illegal Parking remains elevated at 876 complaints over 90 days, indicating systemic parking pressure in district
reporting_angles: Identify the specific streets/blocks where abandoned vehicles are clustering; photograph them for documentation
Contact NYPD Towing and Impound to understand why removal response may be slow; assess whether a single event (e.g., impound facility backlog) triggered the surge

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Dumping complaints jumped to 24 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 5.1 per week—a 368% spike (z-score: 9.61)—indicating environmental crimes concentrated in the past 7–14 days that align with community board's repeated requests for enhanced sanitation resources.
evidence: 24 Illegal Dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (368% increase, z-score: 9.61)
Spike occurred in the week immediately preceding this report, indicating recent problem acceleration
Community board has repeatedly requested more sanitation trucks and equipment, suggesting chronic underfunding of cleanup capacity
reporting_angles: Work with DSNY to map dump sites; visit hotspots to document scale and type of waste (construction debris, household trash, hazmat, etc.)
Interview residents and business owners on specific blocks about whether dumping has worsened; check for any new construction sites that may be driving debris

themes_detail.label: Water Conservation Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Water Conservation complaints reached 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—a rare and sudden surge suggesting possible water main breaks, meter failures, or emergency conservation measures affecting residents this week.
evidence: 3 Water Conservation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
Complaint type is historically rare (0.4/week), making this week's spike statistically extreme
Timing is current-week, suggesting an active problem with water supply or conservation order
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if a water main break, pressure loss, or boil-water advisory triggered complaints in Greenwich Village/SoHo this week
Interview complainants to understand whether they experienced service interruptions, low pressure, or discolored water
